summary: Intermittent 5xx spike during priority rebalancing and IO slab fragmentation
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-12 02:10 UTC we observed repeated 5xx spikes for a subset of NovaChat requests. Errors are concentrated on conversational chat routes for their dedicated cluster and correlate with bursts of priority rebalances triggered by tenant scaling.
impact: Customer-facing: NovaChat reports elevated error rates (~8-12% 5xx) and increased tail latency. Affected endpoints are producing aborted streaming sessions and failed shorter synchronous requests. Business impact: degraded experience for end users and potential SLA breach for dedicated plan.
environment_details: Dedicated capacity pool for NovaChat (dedicated-prod-us-west), pinned model redwood/gemini-13b-v1, autoscaler configured with aggressive warmup. Observed on both us-west and us-east mirror clusters during tenant-reshard event.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate tenant scale-up: push 300 concurrent short-chat requests with mixed priority headers (high/normal)
2) Trigger autoscaler to rebalance shards (force scale-up of ephemeral workers)
3) Observe api-gateway logs and runtime accept-queue metrics for 5-10 minutes
observed_logs_and_traces: apigw ERROR 2026-03-12T02:11:05Z upstream_timeout id=abcd-1234 route=/v1/chat - upstream returned 502
runtime WARN 2026-03-12T02:11:08Z kvcache: io-slab stall detected, reclaiming pages, blocking forward progress
scheduler INFO 2026-03-12T02:11:10Z priority-rebalancer started tenant=novachat action=reshard
runtime ERROR 2026-03-12T02:11:12Z watchdog: worker pid=8421 terminated signal=SIGABRT (OOM?)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: priority rebalancer caused a rapid reassignment of accept-queues which, combined with concurrent small-payload bursts, led to localized IO slab fragmentation and short-lived blocking in the runtime's page reclaim path.
Evidence: stacktraces from terminated worker show repeated page-fault backoff in storage layer; NVMe iostat during window shows transient queue-depth spikes coincident with rebalancer actions.
Correlation: incident timestamps match NovaChat autoscaler events and a delayed keepalive cull on a subset of ephemeral proxies.
SRE partial finding: apigw retries amplified the spike — multiple inflight retries during the short degradation window increased pressure on the runtime and triggered watchdog restarts.
Reproduction attempts: A controlled tenant-reshard test in staging reproduced 5xx floor with similar IO stall symptoms when concurrent high-priority short requests were present.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer reported sudden error rate starting at ~02:10 UTC. Collected traces, request IDs, and example payloads. Escalating to SRE.
Marco Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-12: Gathering runtime logs and iostat. Noticed NVMe queue-depth spikes and multiple SIGABRT from workers. Opening scheduler and runtime threads for deeper trace.

Evelyn Chen (Runtime Eng) 2026-03-12: Stacktrace from worker indicates page_reclaim loop waiting on storage IO; suspect fragmentation in slab allocator exacerbated by many short-lived allocations from high-priority requests.
NovaChat Ops (customer) 2026-03-12: We saw many failed requests in our metrics and temporary client-side retries. We can throttle high-priority traffic during your repro if needed.
Marco Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-13: Applied temporary rate-smoothing rule at API gateway for NovaChat to limit hedged retries and reduce fanout. Error rate dropped to ~1.5% within 7 minutes.
temporary_mitigation: 1) Applied rate-smoothing and hedged-retry suppression at api-gateway for NovaChat tenant during warmup windows.
2) Increased accept-queue depth and delayed aggressive keepalive cull on dedicated proxies for the affected cluster.
3) Disabled an experimental prefetch path for gemini-13b-v1 in the affected pool to reduce short-lived allocations.
permanent_fix_plan: Short-term (24-72h): add backpressure to priority-rebalancer and introduce rate-limits for hedged retries during reshard events; adjust runtime slab allocator thresholds to avoid synchronous page-reclaim under transient NVMe queue pressure.

Medium-term (2-4 weeks): refactor runtime storage allocator to reduce fragmentation for many small allocations; add telemetry that correlates accept-queue reassignments with IO latency spikes for automatic routing to fallback models.
Follow-up: schedule postmortem, update var-runbook for tenant reshards, and propose hotfix to runtime allocator in next minor release.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13: Temporary mitigations brought error rate under SLA. Root cause still under investigation; likely interaction between priority-rebalancer, hedged retries, and IO slab fragmentation.
Customer notified of mitigations and given recommended client-side retry backoff guidance.
Eng to target runtime allocator improvements and scheduler backpressure in upcoming cycles.
